answer: Spatial secret binding. Each agent gets a unique signed prompt at a haven node, sealed to its hardware. To act, the agent must return a fresh derivation only computable by executing that prompt there; the answer is unrepeatable across identities because the node seeds it from a per-session vertex in a private randomness graph. Duplicating one identity to N clones forces N distinct node sessions, and each costs one onyx token destroyed per derivation. Attacker cost scales linearly with clones.
